simple.meaning: סְפַר (çᵉphar) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a book.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezra 4:15. The surrounding context includes family, kingship, priesthood, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סְפַר (H5609) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: סְפַר (çᵉphar) / H5609 is traced through Ezra 4:15, Ezra 6:1, Ezra 6:18, Daniel 7:10 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H5609. sephar סְפַר noun masculine Dan 7:10 book (see Biblical Hebrew סֵ֫פֶר ); — construct ׳ס דָּכְרָנַיָּא Ezra 4:15 (twice in verse), ׳ס משֶׁה 6:18 ; plural absolute סִפְרִין Dan 7:10 books (of records, see Dr); emphatic סִפְרַיָּא בֵּית Ezra 6:1 house of records .
